statement_en: Let $$A_{n}:=\{x:|f_n(x)-f(x)|\geq \varepsilon_n\},$$ where $\varepsilon_n \downarrow 0$, and suppose also that $$\sum_{n\geq 1}\mu(A_n)<\infty.$$ Then if $x \not \in \limsup_{n\to\infty} A_{n}$, there exists $N_x$ such that for all $n >N_x$, $$|f_n(x)-f(x)|< \varepsilon_n.$$ Hence $f_n(x)\to f(x)$, and therefore $$f_n(x)\to f(x)$$ almost everywhere.
